title: Building LLM Features with TypeScript: Structured Output, Tool Calling & Streaming
concept: Put a large language model behind your own API the way you would any unreliable dependency: prompts as versioned contracts, output validated against a schema, bounded retries and fallbacks, tool calls your code checks before running, streaming that survives a broken connection, token budgets per user, and tests that run against fake models and recorded fixtures.
description: An intermediate course for backend developers who are asked to add an AI feature to a real product. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform's AI hint feature - a JSON answer with a missing field that crashed the lesson page, a retry loop that sent the whole repository to the model and multiplied the bill, a tool call with arguments nobody validated, a stream that stopped half-way and left the learner staring at half a sentence, a hint that pasted the reference solution - and fixes it with code you can test without calling a real model: versioned prompt templates, structured output and schema validation, retry and repair with a limit, timeouts, rate limits and provider fallback, safe tool calling, streaming over SSE, token budgets, response caching and testing with fake LLMs. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real prompts, logs and diffs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Treat a prompt as a versioned contract and validate structured output against a schema before using it
Handle invalid output, timeouts, rate limits and broken streams with bounded retries, repair and fallback
Let the model request tools while your code validates the arguments and decides what runs
Keep cost under control with token budgets per user, bounded context and response caching
Keep keys on the server, stop answers that leak solutions, and test LLM features with fake models and fixtures

testedVersions.LLM APIs: provider-agnostic examples with a fake LLM; check current SDK versions

knownIssues: Challenges use a fake LLM and recorded fixtures; calling a real provider and measuring real cost is self-practice
A Python (FastAPI + Pydantic) variant of the labs is planned (V1.3 §6.7) but not written
